text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Romanians would rather invest in housing or keep their money in banks than use the capital market, showed latest opinion survey by local CURS pollster.

- Romania's telephone authority Romtelecom is negotiating with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to get a $200 million credit, half of which would be a syndicated loan and half disbursed by the EBRD, the newspaper says.
- The Romanian Commercial Bank (BCR) has launched the first credit card in the local leu currency.

- The industry ministry plans to lay off 13,000 employees of the Tirgu Jiu mining authority (RAL), 4,000 staff on the payroll of the Baia Mare mining authority and a further 2,000 employed by the Ploiesti mining authority, in exchange for loan tranche from the World Bank to restructure the mining sector.
- Long-delayed efforts to privatise Azomures fertiliser plant and Otelinox stainless steel maker are pointing to the need for changing unwieldy privatisation procedures, the newspaper says.

- The government will not be able to go ahead with plans to lower taxes on wages in August, because it has to stick to the 4.5 percent budget gap benchmark agreed for this year with the International Monetary Fund, the newspaper says.
- The lower Chamber of Deputies has started debates on health insurance law, vital for long-delayed reforms of the health sector.
- One of the two female birds at a new ostrich farm near Baia Mare has weathered the winter and has laid the first eggs, weighing up to 1.6 kg.
- In order to get divorced, Romanians will have to pay 100,000 in a new stamp tax, according to rules on stamp taxes passed by the upper Senate on Tuesday.
